text:
Dylan Strome is doing what Dylan Strome does: making the people around him better shooters. He has 19 points in 22 games, 14 of them assists, and last season Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put his primary shot assists in the 98th percentile among forwards. He also carries the puck into the zone more than half the time, and carry-ins create chances roughly three times as often as dump-ins.

The frustrating part for Washington is the on-ice finishing. The Capitals have scored 5.5 fewer goals than their chances deserved with him out there, which is why his last ten games (7 points) sit a little under what our numbers expected. That kind of gap usually closes.

The trade-off hasn't changed either. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting noticeably more chances with him on the ice last season (bottom 4% of forwards), and his skating speed sits near the bottom of the league. He's a playmaker you build a line around, not a matchup center.
